title: What this teaching asked of women
intro: Heartwood is an invented DVD course. Its teaching is not: every lesson in it comes from booklets and courses sold to women and women's groups between 1987 and 2016. This is what that teaching asked of the women it was sold to, in its own words where it can be quoted.

sections.heading: What it asked of a woman

items.text: To end her closest friendship. When a friendship with another woman became “dependent”, the booklet said “a parting of the ways must take place”, and, where it had been “a lifelong pattern”, that “ties need to be broken with all past partners as well”.
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed p. 24 (PDF p. 30) and p. 20 (PDF p. 28), read on the page images

items.text: To throw away the songs they had shared: the booklet praised getting rid of “certain record albums or tapes (the ones containing ‘our song’)”.
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed p. 25 (PDF p. 30), read on the page image

items.text: To expect the loss to hurt like a marriage ending, and to call it healing: “Prepare for grief and depression. Letting go of a dependent relationship can be as painful as going through a divorce.”
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed p. 25 (PDF p. 30), read on the page image

items.text: To confess her feelings to another Christian, and to give that person “the freedom to periodically ask how things are going”.
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed pp. 22–23 (PDF p. 29), read on the page image

items.text: To watch her friendships for “warning signs”: wanting time alone together, being jealous when the friend sees others, making no plans without her, pet names and private jokes, wearing each other's clothes, poetry or “our song”, moving in together.
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed pp. 8–9 and 15 (PDF pp. 22–25)

items.text: To read the same gestures as sin between two women and as right between a man and a woman: “Romantic gestures and certain kinds of exclusivity are completely appropriate in marriage and engagement … and sometimes even in a serious dating relationship.”
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed pp. 16–17 (PDF p. 26)

sections.heading: Where it told her to look for the cause

items.text: In her mother: a mother “perceived as distant, bitter, critical, overbearing and unloving”, from whom a little girl was said to pull back in “defensive detachment”.
items.source: Focus on the Family, The Heart of the Matter: The Roots and Causes of Female Homosexuality (© 2001), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 6 Folder 4, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 11)

items.text: In her father: “The responses from her father produce the score card of passing or failing as a little girl.”
items.source: Exodus International–North America, Are People Born Gay? (booklet #PR-02, © 1993), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 12, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 6)

items.text: In her family as a whole: her attractions, it said, developed “because of the breakdown in a girl's initial relationship with her family—mother and father”.
items.source: Focus on the Family, The Heart of the Matter: The Roots and Causes of Female Homosexuality (© 2001), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 6 Folder 4, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 10)

items.text: In who she was: “The lesbian struggle is not a sexual orientation problem; it is an identity crisis.”
items.source: Focus on the Family, The Heart of the Matter: The Roots and Causes of Female Homosexuality (© 2001), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 6 Folder 4, printed p. 14 (PDF p. 10)

items.text: In a missing file: “The lesbian woman receives information relating to femininity, but she has no file to put it in.” A 1993 computer analogy; the tape reads it word for word.
items.source: Exodus International–North America, Are People Born Gay? (booklet #PR-02, © 1993), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 12, printed p. 19 (PDF p. 11), read on the page image

items.text: It blamed her. Counsellors, the booklet said, might realise after every kind of help that “this individual has no true interest in changing”.
items.source: Emotional Dependency: A Threat to Close Friendships (InterVarsity Press, 1990; first published by Love in Action, 1984, and by Exodus International–North America, 1987), Smithsonian NMAH.AC.1428 Box 2 Folder 9, printed p. 20 (PDF p. 28), read on the page image

items.text: In June 2016 the dependency booklet was still on sale in fives, for women's groups: “Emotional Dependency, 5 Pack … Package of 5”.
items.source: Exodus Global Alliance, "Women" resources page, archived 11 June 2016, web.archive.org/web/20160611170337/http://www.exodusglobalalliance.org/forwomenp521.php, read 15 Nov 2026

items.text: A church's Living Waters group met on twenty Monday evenings for $150, with payment plans. “Groups fill up in a matter of days.”
items.source: a church counselling centre's "Living Waters" group page, posted 29 March 2016, read 15 Nov 2026 (its address carries a person's name, so it is not printed here)

items.text: Courses like this were sold on DVD, in a Regular Edition and a Leader's Edition with a discussion guide.
items.source: Restored Hope Network, "Suggested Books by Category" (PDF, August 2014), p. 1 (Such Were Some of You, a DVD video curriculum); the Dove review of the same DVD, dove.org/review/10417-such-were-some-of-you/, read 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In May 2012 the World Health Organization's office for the Americas said that homosexuality is not a disorder or an illness, “and therefore it requires no cure”, and that such therapies lack medical justification.
items.source: Pan American Health Organization, "'Cures' for an illness that does not exist" (position statement, May 2012), p. 1; news release 17 May 2012, paho.org/en/news/17-5-2012-therapies-change-sexual-orientation-lack-medical-justification-and-threaten-health, read 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In June 2013 Exodus International announced at its own annual conference that it was closing, and its president apologised.
items.source: Religion News Service in The Christian Century (24 July 2013 issue), christiancentury.org/article/2013-06/ex-gay-group-exodus-international-shuts-down-president-apologizes, read 15 Nov 2026

items.text: In 2014 the Royal College of Psychiatrists said: “There is no sound scientific evidence that sexual orientation can be changed.”
items.source: Royal College of Psychiatrists, Position Statement PS02/2014 (April 2014), p. 2, rcpsych.ac.uk (ps02_2014.pdf), read 15 Nov 2026
